title: Written permission before work on VDOT property
summary: Obtain written VDOT permission before work or nontransportation use on state highways or property under VDOT ownership, control or jurisdiction. Permission extends only to the rights VDOT holds.
evidence: until written permission has been obtained from VDOT

title: Other property interests still require permission
summary: A VDOT permit does not clear other property interests. The permittee must secure other necessary permissions and meet applicable federal, state and local requirements.
evidence: obtaining permission from others who may also have an interest

title: Single-use permit for work at a specific location
summary: The district administrator’s designee issues single-use permits for specific work at a specific location, subject to the stated tree-work exception. The permit also allows repairs and routine maintenance after installation.
evidence: responsible for the issuance of all single use permits

title: Single-use permit for extended traffic interruption
summary: Obtain a single-use permit before stopping or impeding highway travel for more than 15 minutes, or using traffic control that varies from the referenced standard, even when holding districtwide authority.
evidence: Stopping or impeding highway travel in excess of 15 minutes

title: Single-use permit for pavement, shoulder or ditch disturbance
summary: Cutting or disturbing highway pavement, shoulders or ditches requires a single-use permit, even when the activity would otherwise fall under a districtwide permit.
evidence: Cutting or disturbing highway pavement, shoulders, or ditches

title: Single-use permit above the stated cable capacity
summary: Telecommunications service exceeding 100-pair copper cable or the fiber-optic cable diameter equivalent requires a single-use permit. The rule supplies no numeric fiber diameter.
evidence: Installing telecommunication services that exceed 100-pair copper cable

title: Districtwide authority for repeated eligible activities
summary: The central office permit manager issues districtwide permits for eligible repeated activities on nonlimited-access ROW. This is distinct from permission for every installation; single-use triggers still apply.
evidence: central office permit manager shall be responsible for the issuance of all districtwide permits

title: Longitudinal service connection length limit
summary: Under districtwide authority, a longitudinal utility service connection may extend no more than 500 feet, along the outer ROW edge. Cover and as-built conditions also apply.
evidence: not to exceed 500 feet in length

title: Conditional 18-inch cover for telecom service connections
summary: Broadband, telecom and cable television service connections may use at least 18 inches of cover if the permittee accepts the specified damage liability for connections buried with less than 30 inches of cover. This exception applies to service connections under districtwide authority.
feature: Conditional districtwide telecom service connection cover

title: Overlashing allowed under districtwide permit
summary: A districtwide permit permits overlashing onto existing telecom lines or strands unless the work triggers a single-use permit requirement. It does not establish a pole-owner attachment agreement.
evidence: allows for the overlashing of telecommunication lines

title: Agreement for new longitudinal limited-access occupancy
summary: In addition to a single-use permit, new longitudinal occupancy of limited-access ROW or median where none existed requires an agreement under the stated cross-references. Keep this agreement separate from the permit.
evidence: Any new longitudinal occupancy of the limited access right-of-way

title: 36-inch cover where pavement exists
summary: For underground facilities where pavement exists, the rule requires boring, pushing or jacking and at least 36 inches of cover. Other applicable law and permit standards can require more. Do not apply the separate service-connection exception to every underground line.
evidence: Where pavement exists, the permittee shall bore, push, or jack and maintain a minimum cover of 36 inches.
feature: Underground facility cover where pavement exists

title: Utility Company Operations Permit (UP)
summary: Fairfax requires a utility permit for dry utility work in ROW not yet accepted into the VDOT system, county easements or county-owned property. The approved site plan and county control determine the applicable process.
locator: Opening requirements; How Do I Submit My Record?; Review Process
evidence: rights-of-way which have not yet been accepted

title: Traffic control plan for roadway work
summary: The utility permit requirements list a traffic control plan for work performed in the roadway. This is an application requirement; the page does not establish a separate lane-closure permit.
evidence: Traffic control plan (for work performed in the roadway)
